pr_body:
Fix https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/117584. More generally, make queries work where the `LOOKUP JOIN`'s `ON` field makes it into the result.

Also relates https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/116208:
- ~Make `LOOKUP JOIN` work on data nodes.~ **Argh, the multi node tests still have issues and sometimes return `null`** instead of the correctly returned values. But at least the plans sent to data nodes are consistent with the coordinator's plan.
- Solve the item "Look whether the LookupJoin output could be computed inside the class".

**Note to reviewers:** This is not supposed to be a definitive solution for the output order of `LOOKUP JOIN`. That's still open. Accordingly, the updated tests remain minimal; this PR just aims to enable more queries so we can work on more kinds of query plans without running into bugs.

Currently, the computation of a `LookupJoin` node's output happens in the Analyzer; the computed `List<Attribute>` of output attributes is passed on as part of a new `LookupJoin` node. However, then this is replaced by a plain `Join` node in the surrogate step - which forgets about the computed attributes.
This leads to inconsistencies. It also generally prevents execution of lookup joins on data nodes because they are only ever sent `Join` nodes, not `LookupJoin` (the latter is not serializable and doesn't escape the coordinator). This means that the plain `Join` node **must** be the source of truth when it comes to the output, otherwise things will be inconsistent.

Remove the output computation from the Analyzer and move it into the `Join` node, instead.

issue_context.title: ESQL: LOOKUP JOIN's output inconsistent with JOIN's
comments:
This reproduces very nicely when the query does not discard the field that was join **on**; this works as reproducer in the csv test:
```
FROM employees
| SORT emp_no
| LIMIT 3
| EVAL language_code = languages
| LOOKUP JOIN languages_lookup ON language_code
| KEEP emp_no, language_code, language_name
;
```

review_comments: This was used in commented out code, which I presume will never come back?
It will come back - but it's been unused for long now, and it really only wraps 1 line.

This made no sense. And calling `output()` here is bad because `references()` is called in the `fieldNames` method - at which point the `output()` method is illegal to use because it requires a resolved plan.
This test for LOOKUP :chicken: is only reverted to how it was before we added `LOOKUP JOIN`.
